main_text.l: etiam Latinus Scripturarum interpres, Augustinus, Hieronymus, Lucretius, & Virgilius, hoc est, illi ipsi, ex quibus veram simulacri significationem sub etymologiæ specie oppugnat Bellarminus, fortasse nec etymologiam Lactantianam improbant, significationem quidem certè confirmant.

§ Nam, ut de singulis ordine agamus, in Scripturis, inquit, simulacra ubique ponuntur pro idolis: semper enim ubi Latinus interpres posuit simulacra, ut Actorum decimo quinto, Psalmo centesimo decimo tertio, primæ Johannis ultimo, & alibi, semper in Graeco est εἴδωλα. In quibus Bellarmini verbis hoc primò insignitè falsum est, quod tam fidenter asserit iterato semper, semper ubi Latinus interpres posuit simulacra, in Graeco esse εἴδωλα. Nam Latinus interpres posuit simulacra * Actorum decimo septimo, ubi in Graeco, est non εἴδωλα, sed σεβάσματα. Latinus interpres posuit simulacra b Exodi tricesimo quarto, ubi in Graeco est, non εἴδωλα, sed θεοί. Latinus interpres posuit simulacra c Levitici vicesimo sexto, ubi in Graeco est, non εἴδωλα, sed χειροποίητα. Latinus interpres posuit simulacrum d Numerorum vi-cesimo tertio, ubi in Graeco est, non εἴδωλον, sed πόνος. Latinus interpres posuit simulacra in libris e Samuelis, f Regum, & g Chronicorum, ubi Græcè habetur, non εἴδωλα, sed κενοταφια [?], καθαιρέσεις, ὑψηλά [?]. Latinus interpres posuit simulacra in h Esaia, & 30. 13. i Ezekiele, k Hosea, & l Zacharia, ubi Græcè habetur, non εἴδωλα, sed γλυπτά, εἰκόνες, πλανῶντες, τεμένη [?], βδελύγματα [?], στῆλαι [?]. Denique Latinus interpres posuit simulacra m secundo Macca-
a Eod. lib. 2. cap. 5. — reference marks as printed; the Greek and some notes are uncertain, see notes.

page.notes: Reference marks: the printed marks are *, b–m. The note set beside "Esaia" and "Ezekiele" in the scan carries the numbers "& 40.20.", "& 41.29." and "i" in a single block; I was not certain how they map to the words, so the marks i and h are doubtful. Greek words marked [?] (κενοταφια, καθαιρέσεις, ὑψηλά, τεμένη, βδελύγματα, στῆλαι) are doubtful readings from a small, faint scan. The reference "Eod. lib. 2. cap. 5." stands beside the line "in Scripturis", so I placed it there. Text ends with the hyphen of "Macca-" which continues on the next page.
